result:
The patched vector-shader evaluator now matches the Xbox console on every row it targets, and PR #402 is marked ready. It goes to audit because it touches `android/`.

The last session didn't fail. It stopped on purpose while it waited for two device runs, the pgraph must-not-move comparison and the fix build's log. All of those had finished by this resume.

**Results.** Both device runs landed on Thor. Each was scored with `vsh_score.py` against the console's own output:

| capture | before (master) | after (patch) | predicted | lines that matched before and don't now |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SPECIAL_raw | 22/44 | **44/44 (identical)** | 44/44 | 0 |
| SUBNORM_MAC_raw | 11/32 | 11/32 (file unchanged) | 22/32 | 0 |

- **SPECIAL_raw:** every row the patch targets now matches the console: 0×inf and 0×NaN in MUL, MAD, DP3 and DP4, −0×5, RCC(±inf), and NaN through RCP, RCC and RSQ.
- **SUBNORM_MAC_raw missed its prediction by 2 lines.** I predicted 22/32 from an earlier run on Nova, where the evaluator flushed tiny (subnormal) inputs to −0 and the patch then fixes two rows. Thor doesn't flush them, so those two rows never reach the patched rule. The file is byte-identical with and without the patch. The 21 lines still wrong are all subnormal handling, which is issue #255, not this one.
- **Rendering comparison:** I judged it myself with `ab_compare.py` and it passes. All 420 captures are byte-identical with and without the patch. The arms job hasn't posted its own verdict comment yet.
- **Build proof:** the fix build's log doesn't contain the patch-applied line, because Gradle only prints CMake status messages when configure fails. Instead, the build directory still holds the patched source with its marker, written at the time of the fix build. The device rows confirm it too: exactly the 22 targeted lines changed and nothing else did.

**Definition of done:**
- `preflight.sh --allow-tracker` passes.
- The PR's `Files:` line matches the diff.
- The branch merges cleanly into current master.
- `docs/lanes/vshcpu345/NOTES.md` records the results, why the last session ended, and two new things not to repeat: pin the device for subnormal rows, and don't look for CMake status lines in the Gradle log.
- The prediction was registered and committed with its refs in the last session.
- Results are in the PR body and a `[lane.vshcpu345] done:` comment.
- The PR is marked ready.

I also saved a memory note that Thor and Nova differ on this subnormal handling.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in claude.ai's connector settings; they're unavailable until then. This lane didn't need them.
